claim: the river swings west there and the hill ends up facing due south
because: At Tain the Rhône turns east, not west. For a short stretch it flows west to east, and that is why the hill on its east bank faces south. Berry Bros. & Rudd says Hermitage sits on the east bank where the river 'suddenly veers in that direction' at Tain and Tournon. Decanter describes the hill rising 'above a kink in the river as it briefly flows west to east'.
fix: the river swings east there, briefly flowing west to east, and the hill ends up facing due south
